Title: East African Rift
Content: The East African Rift System begins at a location where `text(two)` tectonic plates meet in the Afar region of Africa. The `text(two)` plates that meet at this location are the Arabian Plate to the north and the African Plate to the south. The African Plate is rifting to form `text(two)` new plates.

The Nubian Plate is moving westward and the Somalian Plate is moving eastward relative to the rift. The rift system began approximately `text(25 million years)` ago and now stretches over `text(3000 kilometers)` from the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden down toward the southern tip of Africa. The process of rifting is believed to occur due to heat rising from magma below `text(Earth's)` surface. In `2005`, a part of the crust in the Afar region gave way, spreading the rift area by an additional `text(26 feet)`. This crack was filled with `text(600 billion gallons)` of molten rock, which solidified into basalt.
